name: GitHub
summary: Find GitHub repositories and source code, investigate code behavior, and check issues and pull requests.
description:
**⚠️ SOC 2 review pending — production is blocked until Max and the SOC 2 team sign off.**

Answers questions about a repository's code from GitHub's own search of it: where behavior is implemented, how it handles failures, validation, caching or configuration, with the source excerpts the search returns. Also finds repositories, checks issues and pull requests, and makes changes you confirm on a card.

**What VoiceOS can do on GitHub**
- Get an issue
- Create an issue
- Update an issue (close, reopen, rename, labels, assignees)
- Comment on an issue or pull request
- List pull requests, in one repository or across all of yours
- Review a pull request (comment, approve, or request changes)
- Search repositories
- Search code

**What it can't do:** create, merge or edit pull requests, read pull request diffs or files, list issues, or leave inline review comments.

**Access.** GitHub asks for the `repo` scope: read and write access to your public and private repositories. GitHub can't narrow it further, so VoiceOS limits itself to the eight actions above. Composio stores the GitHub token and may keep logs of requests; check its data retention settings before using private repositories.

**Disconnect.** Turn off **Use my GitHub connection** in Configure. VoiceOS stops using the account and asks Composio to revoke it. Changes already sent to GitHub stay.

blocks.text: 1. Add your Composio project API key

In composio.dev, open Settings → Project Settings → API Keys and paste a project key below. A full-access key works; a scoped one needs Auth configs, Connected accounts and Session management (read and write) and Session tool execution (write). Not a ck_ or uak_ key.
Ask VoiceOS about one of your repositories, click Connect GitHub on the card, and approve access in your browser. GitHub asks for the repo scope.

Keep Ask before every action on. Every change shows a card first; click its button to send it. For now, saying yes won't send a GitHub change, because VoiceOS doesn't pass the card's approval along when you answer by voice.

Say "Show all my PRs", "Show the open pull requests in octocat's Hello-World" or "What's issue 12 in my-org's api repo?" Your own repositories work by name alone. For anyone else's, say the owner the first time; after that, its name alone works until VoiceOS restarts.
Add your organization and repository names to the VoiceOS dictionary so they're transcribed correctly.

tools.description: File a new GitHub issue. Use when the user asks to file or log a bug, task or idea, e.g. 'file a bug in the desktop repo: sign-in freezes after sleep'. The title is the user's words, tidied; body, labels and assignees are optional and come from what they said. VoiceOS shows a confirmation card first and sends the change only when its button is clicked. Returns what was created or changed, with its GitHub link. If GitHub isn't connected, the result is a Connect GitHub card.

owner.description: Repository owner: the user or organization, e.g. 'acme' in github.com/acme/desktop.

repo.description: Repository name, e.g. 'desktop' in github.com/acme/desktop (no .git, no owner).

title.description: Issue title in the user's words.

body.description: Issue description (Markdown). Only what the user said or asked for.

labels.description: Labels to apply, e.g. ['bug']. Only if the user asked; never invent labels.

assignees.description: GitHub logins to assign. Only if the user asked.

confirmation_receipt.description: Leave empty. The confirmation card fills this in when the user approves; calls without it are refused.

/* Custom-card shell (renderCustom): no padding, no gap, no layout opinion —
   the author owns the surface edge to edge. Only the confirm reserve, the
   floated mark, and the corner are the kit's.

   The corner is the kit's because it is not the author's to choose: the host
   cuts the card at --k-radius whatever this document says, so a surface drawn
   at any other radius shows a second edge inside the real one. Carrying it
   here means a card that paints a background or border on this element lands
   on the host's arc for free; a card that paints its own root still has
   var(--k-radius) to name. */
.k-cwrap{position:relative;border-radius:var(--k-radius)}
.k-cwrap.k-confirm{padding-bottom:52px}
.k-mkbar{position:absolute;top:11px;left:13px;z-index:9;display:flex}
/* ---- Surface finish (default-on) ----------------------------------------
   The liquid-glass rim: a 1px hairline with a brighter top edge, drawn as an
   INSET shadow on a fixed overlay so it (a) hugs the visible frame whatever
   height the content settles at, and (b) shares border-radius:var(--k-radius)
   with the host's clip — same arc, drawn inward, so it can neither gap nor
   get shaved by the cutout. This is the same rim recipe the notch's own
   chrome uses. */
.k-rim{position:fixed;inset:0;pointer-events:none;z-index:40;border-radius:var(--k-radius);box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.13),inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,.07)}
html[data-k-theme=light] .k-rim{box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.7),inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.1)}
/* Brand presence (only when the integration declared an accent):
   a soft wash of the brand colour bleeding out of the top-left corner —
   colour the SURFACE, never the mark. The mark stays the bare glyph: a tile
   painted under the logo is chrome the icon didn't ask for, and it reads as
   the harness inventing a colour (see WIDGET_MARK_FLATTEN_HTML in ../ui.ts,
   which strips exactly that tile out of documents generated while the kit
   still drew one). color-mix degrades to no wash on engines without it. */
html[data-k-accent] body{background:radial-gradient(150% 120% at 0% 0%,color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 15%,transparent),transparent 44%) no-repeat}
html[data-k-theme=light][data-k-accent] body{background:radial-gradient(150% 120% at 0% 0%,color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 9%,transparent),transparent 44%) no-repeat}
/* The entrance is OPT-IN, never opt-out. Declaring `animation: … both` from
   opacity:0 and cancelling it under prefers-reduced-motion:reduce means any
   environment that doesn't actually run animations — a headless renderer, a
   paused compositor, a screenshotter — paints an invisible card and never
   recovers. Gating on no-preference makes the un-animated state the readable
   one, so the worst case is a card that simply appears. */
@media(prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference){
.k-wrap>*{animation:k-in .34s cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1) both}
.k-wrap>*:nth-child(2){animation-delay:.04s}
.k-wrap>*:nth-child(3){animation-delay:.08s}
.k-wrap>*:nth-child(n+4){animation-delay:.12s}
}
@keyframes k-in{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(5px)}to{opacity:1;transform:none}}

root.label: Confirm new GitHub issue

tools.name: update_issue
tools.title: Update issue
tools.description: Close, reopen, rename or relabel an issue, rewrite its description, or change its assignees. Use when the user asks to; 'close it' means the issue just discussed. Takes expected_updated_at and issue_title from get_issue. Issues only, not pull requests. VoiceOS shows a confirmation card first and sends the change only when its button is clicked. Returns what was created or changed, with its GitHub link. If GitHub isn't connected, the result is a Connect GitHub card.

owner.description: Repository owner: the user or organization, e.g. 'acme' in github.com/acme/desktop.

repo.description: Repository name, e.g. 'desktop' in github.com/acme/desktop (no .git, no owner).

expected_updated_at.description: updated_at from get_issue for this issue, copied unchanged. Detects edits made while the user was reviewing.

issue_title.description: The issue's current title from get_issue. Shown on the card and checked before sending.

title.description: New title, only if the user asked to rename the issue.

body.description: New description replacing the old one ("" clears it). Only if the user asked.

state.description: 'closed' to close the issue, 'open' to reopen it.

state_reason.description: With state 'closed': completed or not_planned. With state 'open': reopened.

labels.description: Replace ALL labels with exactly this list ([] removes every label).

add_labels.description: Labels to add, keeping the existing ones.

remove_labels.description: Labels to remove, keeping the rest.

assignees.description: Replace ALL assignees with exactly these logins ([] unassigns everyone).

add_assignees.description: Logins to assign, keeping current assignees.

remove_assignees.description: Logins to unassign, keeping the rest.

confirmation_receipt.description: Leave empty. The confirmation card fills this in when the user approves; calls without it are refused.

root.label: Confirm GitHub issue change

tools.name: get_issue
tools.title: Get issue
tools.description: Look up one GitHub issue by number: its title, state, labels, assignees, comments and latest activity. Use when the user asks about an issue, e.g. 'what's issue 12 in the desktop repo?' or 'is 34 still open?'. It reads one issue at a time and can't list or search issues, or find the newest one. Also supplies the updated_at and title that update_issue and create_issue_comment take. Returns the facts as data, each item with its GitHub link, and a card. If GitHub isn't connected, the result is a Connect GitHub card.

owner.description: Repository owner, e.g. 'acme'. Leave it out when the user named only the repository.

repo.description: The repository name as the user said it, e.g. 'desktop' or 'live check'. It is matched against the account's repositories, so a misheard or partial name works.

tools.name: create_issue_comment
tools.title: Comment on issue or PR
tools.description: Post a comment on an issue or a pull request's conversation. Use when the user asks to comment or reply, e.g. 'reply to issue 12 that I can reproduce it on 1.4'. Posts the user's exact words; issue_title comes from get_issue. A conversation comment, not a review or approval. VoiceOS shows a confirmation card first and sends the change only when its button is clicked. Returns what was created or changed, with its GitHub link. If GitHub isn't connected, the result is a Connect GitHub card.

owner.description: Repository owner: the user or organization, e.g. 'acme' in github.com/acme/desktop.

repo.description: Repository name, e.g. 'desktop' in github.com/acme/desktop (no .git, no owner).

issue_number.description: Issue or pull request number to comment on.

issue_title.description: The issue or PR title from get_issue, shown on the card and checked before sending.

body.description: Exact comment text (Markdown), as the user said it.

confirmation_receipt.description: Leave empty. The confirmation card fills this in when the user approves; calls without it are refused.

  if(prior)return prior.signature===signature?prior.promise:Promise.resolve(failure('failed','This requestId already has different arguments.'));
  if(pendingTools.size>=64)return Promise.resolve(failure('failed','Too many pending actions.'));
  var resolve;var promise=new Promise(function(done){resolve=done});
  var timer=setTimeout(function(){pendingTools.delete(id);resolve(failure('unknown','No final response. Check the app before trying again.'))},135000);
  pendingTools.set(id,{resolve:resolve,promise:promise,timer:timer,signature:signature});
  send({type:'voiceos:invokeTool',name:name,args:args,requestId:id});
  return promise;
};
var last=0;
var report=function(){
  /* Never report a collapsed measurement. A frame that is display:none, zero
     width, or in a hidden tab measures ~0, and since the host CLAMPS to 60 and
     we'd then consider that our last known height, one bad sample pins a
     277px card at 60px forever. Staying silent leaves the declared estimate
     in place, which is close to right by construction. */
  if(document.hidden)return;
  var el=document.documentElement;
  if(!el.offsetWidth)return;
  var h=Math.ceil(el.getBoundingClientRect().height);
  if(h<8)return;
  if(Math.abs(h-last)>1){last=h;send({type:'voiceos:resize',height:h})}
};
/* data-voiceos-key is the alias custom markup uses; data-k-key is what the
   kit's own vField emits. Same contract either way. */
var argKey=function(el){
  if(!el||!el.getAttribute)return null;
  return el.getAttribute('data-k-key')||el.getAttribute('data-voiceos-key');
};
addEventListener('message',function(e){
  if(e.source!==parent)return;
  var m=e.data;if(!m)return;
  if(m.type==='voiceos:toolResult'){
    var pending=pendingTools.get(m.requestId);
    if(pending&&['completed','failed','cancelled','unknown'].indexOf(m.status)!==-1){clearTimeout(pending.timer);pendingTools.delete(m.requestId);pending.resolve(m)}
    return;
  }
  if(m.type!=='voiceos:init')return;
  voiceos.canInvokeTools=!!(m.capabilities&&m.capabilities.invokeTool);
  if(m.theme&&m.theme.mode)document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-k-theme',m.theme.mode);
  /* The corner the HOST will actually cut this card at. Same shape as the
     theme leg: the document ships with a correct default and the surface
     corrects it, so a card is never briefly drawn at the wrong radius and
     never depends on the host to send anything. Clamped because the value
     lands in CSS. */
  if(typeof m.radius==='number'&&isFinite(m.radius))document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--k-radius',Math.max(0,Math.min(48,m.radius))+'px');
  var args=m.args||{};
  var fields=document.querySelectorAll('[data-k-key],[data-voiceos-key]');
  for(var i=0;i<fields.length;i++){
    var key=argKey(fields[i]);
    if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(args,key)&&args[key]!=null)fields[i].value=String(args[key]);
  }
  report();
});
document.addEventListener('input',function(e){
  var key=argKey(e.target);
  if(key)send({type:'voiceos:updateInput',key:key,value:e.target.value});
});
document.addEventListener('click',function(e){
  /* Routes BOTH the kit's data-k-link rows and plain <a href="https://…">
     anchors in custom markup out through the host. The sandbox blocks
     navigation anyway, so an unrouted anchor is a click that does nothing. */
  var el=e.target;
  while(el&&el!==document.body){
    if(el.getAttribute&&(el.hasAttribute('data-k-link')||(el.tagName==='A'&&el.hasAttribute('href')))){
      e.preventDefault();
      var href=el.getAttribute('href')||'';
      if(/^https:\/\//i.test(href))send({type:'voiceos:openUrl',url:href});
      return;
    }
    el=el.parentNode;
  }
});
if(window.ResizeObserver){new ResizeObserver(report).observe(document.documentElement)}
addEventListener('load',report);setTimeout(report,0);setTimeout(report,120);
})()</script></body></html>

tools.name: list_pull_requests
tools.title: List pull requests
tools.description: List pull requests in any GitHub repository the account can reach, or one by pull_number: state, author, requested reviewers, description. With no owner or repo: your own open PRs across your repositories. Use when asked about PRs, e.g. 'open PRs in octocat/Hello-World', 'show all my PRs', or what a PR does. Returns descriptions, not diffs. summary_request lets a follow-up add a summary under the card. pull_number also returns head_sha and title, for reviews. Returns the facts as data, each item with its GitHub link, and a card. If GitHub isn't connected, the result is a Connect GitHub card.

owner.description: Repository owner, e.g. 'acme'. Leave it out when the user named only the repository.

repo.description: The repository name as the user said it, e.g. 'desktop' or 'live check'. It is matched against the account's repositories, so a misheard or partial name works. Leave it out, with owner, for the account's own open pull requests across its repositories.

pull_number.description: One pull request number: returns just that PR, in any state, with its head_sha. Use it before reviewing.

presentation_token.description: Copy summary_request.arguments.presentation_token from the preceding result to add your summary beneath its PR card. Reuses those exact facts without another GitHub request.

summary.description: Your one or two short sentences answering the user's question from the returned PR description and metadata. Plain language, no links or file paths. Requires presentation_token; never invent diff details or claim tests passed unless the description says so.

base.description: Only PRs merging into this branch, e.g. 'main'.

head.description: Only PRs from this branch, as 'user:branch' or 'branch'.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Each page is the PRs on the card; for more, repeat the call with page+1.

per_page.description: PRs per page: up to 3, the rows the card shows (default 3). Larger values give 3.

author.description: Optional GitHub login. Keeps only this person's PRs, looking through the 300 most recent that match the other filters. Use only when the user named the author.

tools.name: create_pull_request_review
tools.title: Review pull request
tools.description: Approve a pull request, request changes, or leave a review comment. Use when the user asks for one of those; event is exactly the one they asked for. Takes commit_id (head_sha) and pr_title from list_pull_requests with pull_number. It can't read the diff, so the review text comes from the user. VoiceOS shows a confirmation card first and sends the change only when its button is clicked. Returns what was created or changed, with its GitHub link. If GitHub isn't connected, the result is a Connect GitHub card.

owner.description: Repository owner: the user or organization, e.g. 'acme' in github.com/acme/desktop.

repo.description: Repository name, e.g. 'desktop' in github.com/acme/desktop (no .git, no owner).

event.description: COMMENT, APPROVE, or REQUEST_CHANGES: exactly what the user asked for. Never assume APPROVE.

body.description: Review text written or dictated by the user. Required for COMMENT and REQUEST_CHANGES.

commit_id.description: head_sha of this pull request from list_pull_requests, copied unchanged.

pr_title.description: The PR title from list_pull_requests. Shown on the card and checked against GitHub before sending.

confirmation_receipt.description: Leave empty. The confirmation card fills this in when the user approves; calls without it are refused.

:root{--ink-1:rgba(255,255,255,.95);--ink-2:rgba(255,255,255,.72);--ink-3:rgba(255,255,255,.5);--ink-4:rgba(255,255,255,.42);--line:rgba(255,255,255,.08);--fill-1:rgba(255,255,255,.06);--fill-2:rgba(255,255,255,.1);--track:rgba(255,255,255,.12);--good:#30d158;--bad:#ff453a;--accent:#3987e5;--k-radius:26px;color-scheme:dark}

/* Custom-card shell (renderCustom): no padding, no gap, no layout opinion —
   the author owns the surface edge to edge. Only the confirm reserve, the
   floated mark, and the corner are the kit's.

   The corner is the kit's because it is not the author's to choose: the host
   cuts the card at --k-radius whatever this document says, so a surface drawn
   at any other radius shows a second edge inside the real one. Carrying it
   here means a card that paints a background or border on this element lands
   on the host's arc for free; a card that paints its own root still has
   var(--k-radius) to name. */
.k-cwrap{position:relative;border-radius:var(--k-radius)}
.k-cwrap.k-confirm{padding-bottom:52px}
.k-mkbar{position:absolute;top:11px;left:13px;z-index:9;display:flex}
/* ---- Surface finish (default-on) ----------------------------------------
   The liquid-glass rim: a 1px hairline with a brighter top edge, drawn as an
   INSET shadow on a fixed overlay so it (a) hugs the visible frame whatever
   height the content settles at, and (b) shares border-radius:var(--k-radius)
   with the host's clip — same arc, drawn inward, so it can neither gap nor
   get shaved by the cutout. This is the same rim recipe the notch's own
   chrome uses. */
.k-rim{position:fixed;inset:0;pointer-events:none;z-index:40;border-radius:var(--k-radius);box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.13),inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,.07)}
html[data-k-theme=light] .k-rim{box-shadow:inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.7),inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.1)}
/* Brand presence (only when the integration declared an accent):
   a soft wash of the brand colour bleeding out of the top-left corner —
   colour the SURFACE, never the mark. The mark stays the bare glyph: a tile
   painted under the logo is chrome the icon didn't ask for, and it reads as
   the harness inventing a colour (see WIDGET_MARK_FLATTEN_HTML in ../ui.ts,
   which strips exactly that tile out of documents generated while the kit
   still drew one). color-mix degrades to no wash on engines without it. */
html[data-k-accent] body{background:radial-gradient(150% 120% at 0% 0%,color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 15%,transparent),transparent 44%) no-repeat}
html[data-k-theme=light][data-k-accent] body{background:radial-gradient(150% 120% at 0% 0%,color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 9%,transparent),transparent 44%) no-repeat}
/* The entrance is OPT-IN, never opt-out. Declaring `animation: … both` from
   opacity:0 and cancelling it under prefers-reduced-motion:reduce means any
   environment that doesn't actually run animations — a headless renderer, a
   paused compositor, a screenshotter — paints an invisible card and never
   recovers. Gating on no-preference makes the un-animated state the readable
   one, so the worst case is a card that simply appears. */
@media(prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference){
.k-wrap>*{animation:k-in .34s cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1) both}
.k-wrap>*:nth-child(2){animation-delay:.04s}
.k-wrap>*:nth-child(3){animation-delay:.08s}
.k-wrap>*:nth-child(n+4){animation-delay:.12s}
}
@keyframes k-in{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(5px)}to{opacity:1;transform:none}}

tools.title: Search repositories
tools.description: Find GitHub repositories, public and private. Use when the user asks to find repositories, e.g. 'my Python repos'. Owner, language, visibility and sort carry through, include_forks true adds forks, and per_page sets the count. Returns the total and up to five rows at a time, exactly the card's rows in its order; next.arguments continues the same search. Returns the facts as data, each item with its GitHub link, and a card. If GitHub isn't connected, the result is a Connect GitHub card.

q.description: New search only: preserve owner, language and visibility qualifiers. For 'my repositories', reuse the known GitHub owner; ask if unknown. Omit q when using cursor.

cursor.description: For 'next five' or 'next page', copy next.arguments.cursor from the preceding result. Send cursor alone; it preserves the exact query, filters, sort and displayed position.

include_forks.description: Set true when the user asks to include forks (adds fork:true), false to exclude them. Leave visibility unfiltered to include both public and private repositories.

sort.description: Sort by stars, forks, help-wanted-issues, updated, or created. Omit for best match.

order.description: desc or asc; only used with sort.

per_page.description: Page size, 1-100 (default 5). Use the requested count, e.g. 5 for 'five'. The card and result show at most five at a time; next preserves the undisplayed rows.

tools.name: search_code
tools.title: Search code
tools.description: Find code in GitHub repositories. Use when asked where code lives or how it behaves. With repo:owner/name in q it searches that repository; without it, every repository the account can see, private ones included. intent explain returns code excerpts for implementation questions. next.arguments continues the search. Returns the facts as data, each item with its GitHub link, and a card. If GitHub isn't connected, the result is a Connect GitHub card.

q.description: Search terms plus repo:owner/name for the intended repository. This is REST code search: use literal terms, not symbol: or content:. Fork search may miss files even on the default branch. Omit q when using cursor.

cursor.description: For more results, copy next.arguments.cursor and send cursor alone. Preserves the query and displayed position.

intent.description: Use explain for implementation questions or requested code snippets. Use returned fragments, or read a returned public source_url with VoiceOS's web reader. Never infer behavior from names. Private source without fragments is unavailable. At most one search refinement.

per_page.description: Page size, 1-100 (default 5). Use the requested count; the result and card show at most five rows together.
